### STM32 Bare-Metal Mastery — v4
A curriculum for one person, one desk, and two boards (three if you count the second G431KB). **266 items · 6 phases · 5 gates with capstone (+1 optional) · ≈704 h net work.**
Replaces v2, v2.3, v2.4, and v3. Retains from v3 what worked (phases, PASS/GAP, ◈, capstones) and fixes what was broken or missing.
**How this file is built:** numbering, ranges per phase, and totals are generated by a script from the items. Therefore, they can no longer drift out of sync.
#### What changed compared to v3
**Bugs fixed**
* The unaligned access item stated that it "fails on M7". A regular unaligned LDR/STR does not fail on M4/M7. It is now triggered with CCR.UNALIGN_TRP or with LDRD/LDM (Level 16).
* The "timer double clock" item was reversed. The timer clock is doubled when the APB prescaler is **different from 1** (Level 9).
* Stop 2 does not exist on G4. Stop 0/Stop 1, Standby, and Shutdown are now used (Level 18). Verify in RM0440.
* Capstone D required M7 cache and Stop on the same board. Now it is a CAN node across two G431KB boards, and cache moves to Phase 6.
* Fixed the erroneous citation "Little" to Barr Group, *Embedded C Coding Standard*.
* Removed dependence on HSE (Nucleo-32 may lack an HSE crystal): calibrated against LSE.
**Gaps closed**
* Host tests and CI from Level 2, not from 229.
* Minimal UART TX before Capstone B, which needed it without teaching it.
* New levels: state machines, ADC, internal flash and persistent configuration, fixed-point and control (PID).
* Hardware CRC, tickless with RTOS, and current measurement strategy.
**Less friction**
* Each item has an S/M/L size, and each level ends with a reusable **block** (like the UART or FIFO in the FPGA roadmap).
* Removed glossary, exemptions, maintenance mode, and evidence forms.
* Gate review reduced from 10 items to 3.
* Verification, static analysis, and CI condensed into a single level.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### 0. How it works
##### 0.1 Rules
1. One item at a time. Within a phase, in order. Within a level, the order is free.
2. Each item leaves an artifact in evidence/NNN/ (screenshot, log, map excerpt, diff, test result) and one line in notes/NNN.md with what surprised you.
3. An item is **PASS** ("Done when" is met and the artifact proves it) or **GAP** (something is missing; write what in one line and return later). A GAP is a pending task, not a judgment.
4. **◈** marks an item where you must also **provoke the fault and observe it**. A ◈ without a fault artifact is a GAP even if the feature works.
5. **Block** (final item of a level): leaves a reusable module in drivers/ or src/, with host tests and its contract documented in the header.
6. Build from command line. No IDE projects that you cannot rebuild from scratch.
7. Stuck for more than 90 minutes: write down the state, stop, and return tomorrow.
8. If you already master an item, complete it in one sitting with its artifact and move on. Do not re-study.
9. Read Appendix A before each phase and review Appendix B (instrumentation) before starting it.
##### 0.2 Sizes
| Size | Effort | Hours used in estimate |
| ------ | ------ | ------ |
| **S** | one sitting, ≤ 1 h | 0.75 |
| **M** | half day, 2–4 h | 3 |
| **L** | 1–4 days; includes all blocks | 12 |

If the topic is new to you, multiply by 1.5. An L item that drags on for more than a week must be split and not dragged along further.
##### 0.3 Gates
A phase ends when all three conditions are met:
* the capstone is in PASS;
* three items from that phase, chosen at random, are redone **without notes and on hardware**, and all three pass (otherwise, the gate waits one week);
* no GAPs remain in the phase.
Reading the next phase is always allowed.
**Items impossible with your hardware:** write "N/A: reason" in notes/ and do the substitute indicated in the item itself or the closest equivalent. Maximum 3 per phase.
##### 0.4 Weekly review
Once a week, 10 minutes: redo a random item from a previous phase. If it got rusty, this will catch it.
##### 0.5 If you fall behind
Slow down to one item per day. Never skip a level.
##### 0.6 Repository
```
stm32/
  notes/NNN.md
  evidence/NNN/
  src/            application
  board/          board layer (g431kb, host)
  drivers/        peripherals and blocks
  linker/
  startup/
  test/           host tests
  tools/          scripts (decoders, reproducers)
  docs/           pin maps, wire formats, CAN catalog, budgets
  .github/workflows/
  build.sh
  test.sh
```
##### 0.7 Hardware
| Part | Purpose | From |
| ------ | ------ | ------ |
| NUCLEO-G431KB (CM4F, 170 MHz, 128 KB flash, 32 KB SRAM, FDCAN) | primary board | Phase 1 |
| Second NUCLEO-G431KB | CAN node, pulse/PWM generator for your tests, UART node | Phase 3 |
| 8-channel logic analyzer with decoders | almost everything | Phase 2 |
| Multimeter | voltage levels, continuity | Phase 2 |
| Oscilloscope (optional, 3 items for rise times and reflections) | alternative indicated in each item | Phase 2 |
| 1 SPI sensor with WHO_AM_I and 1 I2C sensor (inexpensive breakouts) | Phase 3 | Phase 3 |
| 2 3.3V CAN transceivers and 2 120 Ω terminators | CAN | Phase 4 |
| µA meter with logging (Nordic PPK2 or equivalent) | low power | Phase 4 |
| NUCLEO-H755ZI-Q | Phase 6 only, optional | Phase 6 |

**Warning:** the Nucleo-32 may lack an IDD jumper for current measurement. Verify in the board manual (UM2397) and plan to power the MCU externally in Level 18.
##### 0.8 Phases
| Phase | Levels | Items | Qty | Capstone | Approx. Hours |
| ------ | ------ | ------ | ------ | ------ | ------ |
| 1 — Language and build | 1–3 | 001–037 | 37 | Capstone A | 62 |
| 2 — Pins, timing, interrupts and first serial | 4–8 | 038–087 | 50 | Capstone B | 125 |
| 3 — Timers, analog, buses and persistence | 9–14 | 088–152 | 65 | Capstone C | 182 |
| 4 — DMA, core, CAN, power and booting | 15–19 | 153–209 | 57 | Capstone D | 176 |
| 5 — Control, RTOS and quality | 20–24 | 210–254 | 45 | Capstone E | 119 |
| 6 — Dual-core and cache (optional) | 25–25 | 255–266 | 12 | Capstone F | 40 |

≈704 h in total; at 10 h/week ≈70 weeks, at 15 h/week ≈47. If the topic is new to you, multiply by 1.5.
Phase 6 is optional until you have a real reason for it. Everything preceding it is not.

#### Phase 1 — Language and build
Foundations. Without this, the rest is copying from CubeMX with extra steps.
##### Level 1 — C that bites in embedded
**Prerequisite:** none. **Verified with:** host gcc, nm, objdump, sanitizers.
* **001** S Store module state with static storage duration when it must survive the frame. — *Done when:* a module keeps state at file scope and no pointer to it escapes before initialization.
* **002** S Make state private with static and expose access only through functions. — *Done when:* nm shows no exported symbols that you did not intend to export.
* **003** M Replace a register or protocol bitfield with masks and shifts. — *Done when:* a host test fixes offsets and passes with -O0 and -O2.
* **004** M Create field macros (_POS, _MSK, GET, SET) to read and write multi-bit fields without touching the rest. — *Done when:* a test exercises them with patterns 0x00000000 and 0xFFFFFFFF and neighboring bits do not change.
* **005** S Track integer promotion of char and short within expressions. — *Done when:* you declare the promoted type of three of your expressions and -Wconversion confirms it.
* **006** M Eliminate signed/unsigned mixing and implicit narrowing (uint8_t x; x += 200;). — *Done when:* the build is clean with -Wsign-compare -Wsign-conversion -Wconversion and each narrowing is an explicit cast or a wider intermediate.
* **007** S ◈ Provoke a signed overflow (INT32_MAX + 1) and compare -O0 with -O2. — *Done when:* the result diverges, you capture it, and explain the root cause in one line.
* **008** S Use volatile only where the compiler cannot know better: ISR flags, registers, memory-mapped state. — *Done when:* you remove two decorative volatiles without breaking anything and the -O2 disassembly shows a busy-wait that disappeared without volatile.
* **009** S Measure struct padding, reorder members, and lock size with _Static_assert (size, offsets, alignment, enum range; at least five assumptions). — *Done when:* a layout or type change breaks the build with a clear error message.
* **010** S Parse a byte buffer with memcpy, without pointer casts. — *Done when:* the parser runs cleanly under -fsanitize=undefined,address on host.
* **011** S Write explicit serialization of uint16_t/uint32_t in little and big endian. — *Done when:* a host test verifies both byte orders and is independent of host endianness.
* **012** S Place const correctly: const char *, char * const, const char * const. — *Done when:* you fix three existing signatures and the intent is unambiguous.
* **013** M Dispatch via function pointer table instead of switch. — *Done when:* a table of five handlers dispatches correctly and nm/objdump places it in .rodata.
* **014** S Propagate errors by value (enum status_t) across three call levels. — *Done when:* no error is dropped without return or logging (-Wunused-result monitors it).
* **015** M Replace malloc with a static fixed-block pool. — *Done when:* 1000 alloc/free cycles without fragmentation, exhaustion is reported cleanly, and no malloc appears in the link.
##### Level 2 — Host testing and CI from day one
**Prerequisite:** Level 1. **Verified with:** ./test.sh, the pipeline.
* **016** S Choose a minimal runner (Unity or 30 custom lines with assert). — *Done when:* ./test.sh runs Level 1 tests and returns non-zero if one fails.
* **017** S Compile tests with -Wall -Wextra -Wconversion -Werror and sanitizers. — *Done when:* a deliberate sanitizer failure breaks the test.
* **018** M Create a CI workflow that runs ./test.sh on every push. — *Done when:* a push with a broken test turns red and is blocked.
* **019** S ◈ Add cppcheck (or clang-tidy) to CI with findings that break the build. — *Done when:* an issue introduced intentionally breaks the CI.
* **020** S Write a regression test **before** fixing a real bug from Level 1. — *Done when:* the test fails before the fix and passes after, in separate commits.
##### Level 3 — Toolchain, startup and linker
**Prerequisite:** Level 2. **Verified with:** .map, size, sha256sum, clean tree.
* **021** S Pin the arm-none-eabi-gcc toolchain version and compile with -mcpu=cortex-m4 -mthumb -mfloat-abi=hard -mfpu=fpv4-sp-d16. — *Done when:* readelf -A confirms architecture and the version is recorded in README and CI.
* **022** M Read ST's reference linker script and annotate each region (FLASH, SRAM1, SRAM2, CCM). — *Done when:* each region has annotated size and contents, verified against RM0440.
* **023** M Write your own linker script for G431KB (128 KB flash, 32 KB RAM, separate CCM). — *Done when:* the build links and size matches the map.
* **024** S Place the vector table in flash at the correct address. — *Done when:* .isr_vector appears at 0x08000000 in the map and reset functions properly.
* **025** M Write your own startup: reset handler, copy .data, zero .bss, main. — *Done when:* a global initialized to 7 is 7 in main and an uninitialized global is 0.
* **026** M ◈ Enable the FPU at reset (CPACR) before any float code runs. — *Done when:* a floating-point operation executes; removing activation triggers a UsageFault you capture.
* **027** S ◈ Enable -ffunction-sections -fdata-sections --gc-sections. — *Done when:* deleting a call shrinks the map and no orphaned sections remain.
* **028** S Read a .map file: locate a symbol, its section, and its size. — *Done when:* you find three symbols of your choice and declare their region.
* **029** S Compare the size of two builds and attribute the difference. — *Done when:* size and the map explain the difference line by line.
* **030** S ◈ Compile with -O2 -g3 -Wall -Wextra -Wconversion -Wsign-conversion -Werror. — *Done when:* the build is clean and intentional narrowing breaks it.
* **031** M Make the build reproducible: fixed SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH, sorted inputs, no timestamps in strings. — *Done when:* two clean builds are identical under sha256sum.
* **032** M Reduce the build to a single command from a clean tree. — *Done when:* git clean -xdf plus ./build.sh produces a working binary.
* **033** S Embed semantic version and build ID into their own section in the binary. — *Done when:* strings/objdump show them, version increments with a tag, and ID changes on any source edit. (Printing them at boot is reserved for Level 6.)
* **034** M Choose an assertion strategy: trap with file and line in debug, compiled out in release, never assert() on a recoverable condition. — *Done when:* a forced assertion halts in debugger with location and release contains no assertion code (objdump).
* **035** S ◈ Enforce a binary size budget. — *Done when:* exceeding it breaks the build.
* **036** M Flash and debug from the command line (OpenOCD + GDB). — *Done when:* ./build.sh flash and ./build.sh debug work without an IDE.
* **037** M Isolate board differences in board/: app/ compiles unmodified for G431KB and for a host "board" with stubs. — *Done when:* app/ compiles for both, host version runs inside ./test.sh.
##### Gate 1 — Capstone A
**Dual-blink from an empty tree.** Two independent blinking modules from an empty directory: your linker script, your startup, your build script, reproducible and under size budget. One blinks at 1 Hz and the other at 3 Hz with 30% duty. Neither uses a hardware timer, only SysTick. Uses the on-board LED and an external LED on a second pin (Nucleo-32 has only one user LED). **Done when:** both blink, build is reproducible, size is under budget, and timing logic has at least one host test passing in CI. **Prohibited:** CubeMX output, IDE project files, HAL_Delay, a clock divider shared between modules.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Phase 2 — Pins, timing, interrupts and first serial
##### Level 4 — Clock and GPIO
**Prerequisite:** Gate 1. **Verified with:** logic analyzer, datasheet, register dumps.
* **038** M Trace the clock tree from HSI/HSE to a peripheral bus. — *Done when:* clock tree is drawn with each prescaler and mux along the path labeled.
* **039** M Configure the PLL to 170 MHz (with correct flash latency and power mode per RM0440) and verify via MCO divided by a prescaler your analyzer can measure. — *Done when:* analyzer measures expected frequency on MCO.
* **040** S ◈ Increase frequency without adjusting flash latency. — *Done when:* you observe the fault (hard fault or erratic behavior), capture it, and correct it.
* **041** S Enable peripheral GPIO clock in RCC and disable it. — *Done when:* the pin responds with clock and stops responding without it.
* **042** M Explicitly configure mode, speed, pull, and output type for every pin you use. — *Done when:* a register dump of your init shows no unreviewed default fields.
* **043** S Drive an output using BSRR/BRR and explain why it is atomic. — *Done when:* two pins toggle with one instruction each and disassembly contains no read-modify-write.
* **044** S Poll a pin via IDR and measure latency with DWT->CYCCNT. — *Done when:* you report the cycle count.
* **045** S Configure a pin as alternate function using the AF number from the datasheet table. — *Done when:* AF field matches table and signal appears.
* **046** S Configure a pin as analog (disconnect digital buffer). — *Done when:* you measure current or noise with and without buffer and explain that it is not isolation.
* **047** M Drive an open-drain pin with an external pull-up. — *Done when:* line rises when released and you document rise time (oscilloscope; without it, calculate RC and verify level on analyzer).
* **048** S Compare two slew rates on the same net. — *Done when:* two captures are compared.
* **049** S ◈ Respect BOOT0 and SWD pins: never reconfigure them blindly. — *Done when:* board remains debuggable after your init. (Verify board manual for which pin shares boot function with your LED.)
* **050** M Write the pin map: pin, function, AF, direction, pull, and the constraint that forced it. — *Done when:* someone could reconstruct your wiring using only this document.
* **051** S Control an LED and a button behind an abstraction without register names in main. — *Done when:* main calls led_on() and button_pressed().
##### Level 5 — Timing, NVIC and EXTI
**Prerequisite:** Level 4. **Verified with:** logic analyzer, cycle counter.
* **052** S Use SysTick as a monotonic millisecond counter. — *Done when:* advances at 1 kHz on analyzer and DWT confirms within ±1%.
* **053** S ◈ Handle counter wrap in timeout comparisons. — *Done when:* a timeout survives 2^32 wrap (host test with simulated time and on-board forcing initial value).
* **054** M Write non-blocking delay_ms that does not block interrupts. — *Done when:* an ISR continues firing during a 500 ms delay.
* **055** S Set NVIC priority grouping and purposefully assign preemption and subpriority. — *Done when:* you explain choice and its consequence.
* **056** M Configure an EXTI line on a button with pull-up and software debouncing. — *Done when:* 50 presses produce exactly 50 events.
* **057** S Keep the ISR to a flag and do the work in main loop. — *Done when:* ISR body has fewer than ten instructions in disassembly.
* **058** S ◈ Forget to clear the EXTI pending bit and observe continuous re-triggering. — *Done when:* you capture the behavior and handler fires once per edge after fixing it.
* **059** M Measure interrupt latency from edge to first instruction of ISR. — *Done when:* you report the number and configuration that produced it.
* **060** M ◈ Give a real-time source highest preemption and a background task lowest; demonstrate priority inversion and fix it by assigning priorities. — *Done when:* inversion is reproducible before fix and disappears after.
* **061** S Measure length of a critical section in cycles. — *Done when:* window is measured.
* **062** M ◈ Detect a missed deadline: a flag still active when the next event arrives. — *Done when:* overload increments a counter visible in debugger (logging arrives in Level 6).
* **063** L **Block:** Timebase module: now_ms(), deadline_after(), deadline_expired(), with host tests covering wrap. — *Done when:* tests pass in CI and Capstone A uses the module.
##### Level 6 — Minimal UART TX and logging
**Prerequisite:** Level 5. **Verified with:** logic analyzer, serial terminal.
* **064** M Configure USART connected to ST-LINK VCP at 115200 8N1 with blocking byte-by-byte transmission. — *Done when:* you see bytes in terminal and analyzer decodes 115200.
* **065** S Calculate BRR, measure real baudrate and its error. — *Done when:* you report percentage error and it falls within receiver tolerance.
* **066** M Write a bounded log_printf with levels (ERR/WARN/INFO/DBG) and now_ms() timestamp. — *Done when:* DBG level compiles to zero bytes in release and you measure cycle cost of one line.
* **067** S Evaluate cost of %f support in printf (newlib-nano). — *Done when:* you measure flash delta and decide whether to enable it.
* **068** S Print version, build ID, and reset cause (RCC->CSR) at boot. — *Done when:* you distinguish power-on reset from reset pin.
##### Level 7 — Basic concurrency
**Prerequisite:** Level 6. **Verified with:** stress tests, analyzer, threaded host test.
* **069** M ◈ Show that volatile is not atomic: an ISR increments a volatile uint32_t while main decrements it. — *Done when:* you measure drift and capture it.
* **070** M ◈ Fix drift with a critical section (PRIMASK/BASEPRI) or C11 atomics, and explain why volatile failed. — *Done when:* drift is 0 in 10^6 cycles.
* **071** S Enumerate shared state between each ISR and main. — *Done when:* each object is listed with its writer and reader.
* **072** M Implement a lock-free SPSC ring buffer with head and tail indices. — *Done when:* 10^6 transfers without loss or corruption (host test with two threads and on board).
* **073** S Make capacity a power of 2 and wrap with a mask. — *Done when:* disassembly has no divisions and code is shorter.
* **074** M ◈ Distinguish full from empty unambiguously. — *Done when:* a full buffer rejects cleanly, an empty one returns a sentinel, and neither reads as valid data.
* **075** S Detect producer overflow without blocking the ISR. — *Done when:* an overflow counter increments and consumer logs the loss.
* **076** M Use double buffering when producer must always finish writing. — *Done when:* consumer never sees a torn frame.
* **077** S Apply compiler or memory barrier (__DMB, atomic_signal_fence) where ordering matters. — *Done when:* you name the reordering that breaks without it.
* **078** M ◈ Intentionally leave consumer unattended. — *Done when:* producer remains healthy and overflow path is exercised.
* **079** S Document concurrency contract of each shared object in its header. — *Done when:* each declares writer, reader, and guarantee.
* **080** L **Block:** Generic static ringbuf module with host tests. — *Done when:* passes in CI and log or UART can use it.
##### Level 8 — State machines in C
**Prerequisite:** Level 7. **Verified with:** host tests. (Equivalent to FSM level in FPGA roadmap.)
* **081** M Implement an FSM with enum and switch detecting "short-short-long" button sequence. — *Done when:* each state and transition has a test.
* **082** M Rewrite FSM as a table (state × event → action, next). — *Done when:* same suite passes and you compare size and readability.
* **083** M Build debounce as an FSM on top of timebase without blocking delays. — *Done when:* simulated bounces on host and real on board: 50 presses give 50 events.
* **084** M ◈ Handle illegal events: every undefined (state, event) pair transitions to a logged error state, not ignored. — *Done when:* injecting an illegal event increments a counter and logs.
* **085** M Add state timeouts using deadlines. — *Done when:* timeout triggers on the correct tick, even across wrap.
* **086** M Create a run-to-completion event queue: ISRs publish and a dispatcher processes. — *Done when:* button FSM and timeout FSM share the dispatcher without blocking.
* **087** L **Block:** Reusable fsm, debounce, and button modules with tests. — *Done when:* pass in CI and Capstone B uses them.
##### Gate 2 — Capstone B
**Button-to-event pipeline.** A debounced button (FSM) produces timestamped events into the ringbuf. A consumer drains them, formats via log, and prints through Level 6 UART TX. Dropped events are counted and reported. Interrupt latency is measured and declared. **Done when:** 100 presses produce 100 events without loss, latency figure is in notes/, and FSM and ringbuf have CI tests. **Prohibited:** busy-waiting on the button, consumer polling slower than a tick, or dropping an event silently.

#### Phase 3 — Timers, analog, buses and persistence
Here the work shifts from "making things blink" to "moving real data."
##### Level 9 — Timers
**Prerequisite:** Gate 2. **Verified with:** analyzer (oscilloscope if available), second board as pulse generator.
* **088** S Configure a basic timer with periodic interrupt. — *Done when:* a pin toggling in ISR shows the configured ARR period on the analyzer.
* **089** S Calculate PSC and ARR for a target frequency and declare rounding error. — *Done when:* error is under 0.1% or justified.
* **090** M Use input capture to measure pulse width. — *Done when:* 1 ms pulse generated by second board measures 1 ms ±1 tick.
* **091** M Generate PWM sweeping duty cycle from 0 to 100%. — *Done when:* analyzer measures duty and 0% and 100% extremes are glitch-free.
* **092** M ◈ Resolve timer double clock: with APB prescaler != 1, timer clock is 2×PCLK. — *Done when:* a frequency came out double due to this cause, and you fix it.
* **093** M Read a quadrature encoder (real or simulated by second board). — *Done when:* count increments and decrements when direction is reversed.
* **094** M Trigger slave timer from master update (master/slave) to generate a single delayed pulse. — *Done when:* offset is fixed and measured.
* **095** M Generate complementary PWM with dead time. — *Done when:* analyzer shows dead time between edges and value matches configuration.
* **096** M ◈ Capture at 10 kHz without dropping edges for one minute. — *Done when:* transmitted edge count matches captured edge count.
* **097** M ◈ Use independent watchdog (IWDG) as deadline detector: only healthy path refreshes it. — *Done when:* stuck loop causes reset and log identifies cause.
* **098** M Calibrate HSI against LSE (or HSE if your board has it) via timer capture. — *Done when:* you report deviation in ppm.
##### Level 10 — ADC
**Prerequisite:** Level 9. **Verified with:** multimeter, potentiometer, second board, or known voltage divider.
* **099** M Perform single software conversion on a known resistive divider. — *Done when:* reading matches measured voltage and error is quantified in LSBs.
* **100** S Read Vrefint and calculate actual VDDA; convert to volts using factory calibration. — *Done when:* converted voltage matches multimeter within quantified error.
* **101** S Run ADC self-calibration before use. — *Done when:* you measure offset with and without calibration.
* **102** M ◈ Select sampling time based on source impedance and demonstrate error with too short time on high-impedance source. — *Done when:* error is visible and corrected with longer time.
* **103** M Trigger conversion from timer and handle end-of-conversion in ISR. — *Done when:* sample instants align with timer without software trigger.
* **104** M Scan multiple channels with circular DMA into a buffer. (First DMA usage; Level 15 explores deeper.) — *Done when:* known signal lands at expected buffer offset without CPU intervention.
* **105** M Apply hardware or software oversampling and measure noise on a fixed input. — *Done when:* standard deviation drops by expected ratio and effective bits gained is reported.
* **106** S Read internal temperature sensor and convert to °C with factory calibration. — *Done when:* reading is reasonable compared to thermometer (±3 °C).
* **107** M ◈ Use analog watchdog to trigger ISR upon threshold crossing. — *Done when:* ISR fires on crossing and re-arms.
* **108** L **Block:** Module adc_drv returning millivolts, with calibration and per-channel sample time selection. — *Done when:* passes host test with simulated ADC and Capstone C uses it.
##### Level 11 — Full UART and protocols
**Prerequisite:** Levels 7 and 10. **Verified with:** analyzer and second board.
* **109** M Configure UART with DMA RX into circular buffer, using ringbuf if suitable. — *Done when:* 1 kB/s for one minute without overrun.
* **110** M ◈ Handle idle line, framing, and overrun: force each and report. — *Done when:* each error is reported and none is ignored.
* **111** M Create framing layer: start byte, length, payload, and CRC. — *Done when:* corrupted frame is rejected and good frame is delivered.
* **112** S Calculate CRC-16 (CCITT) in software and verify on both ends. — *Done when:* exhaustive host test confirms any single-bit flip is detected.
* **113** S Use hardware CRC peripheral and compare against software version. — *Done when:* results match and cycle count of each is reported.
* **114** M ◈ Make parser resynchronize after injected garbage. — *Done when:* after random garbage, parser recovers valid frames within at most one frame.
* **115** M ◈ Fuzz test parser on host with random and mutated inputs. — *Done when:* 10^6 inputs without crash or out-of-bounds read under sanitizers.
* **116** M ◈ Detect absent peer using link timeout. — *Done when:* disconnecting peer triggers link-down within timeout.
* **117** S Version the protocol and reject unknown versions with explicit error. — *Done when:* unknown version frame yields expected error.
* **118** M ◈ Handle full TX queue without blocking caller. — *Done when:* policy (drop or backpressure) is declared and exercised.
* **119** S Measure throughput ceiling and identify limiting factor. — *Done when:* you report number and bottleneck.
* **120** S Document wire format with offsets and endianness. — *Done when:* another engineer could build a peer without talking to you.
* **121** L **Block:** Modules uart_drv, frame, and crc with host tests including fuzzing. — *Done when:* pass in CI and Capstone C uses them.
##### Level 12 — SPI and I2C
**Prerequisite:** Level 11. **Verified with:** analyzer with protocol decoders and datasheets.
* **122** M Configure SPI clock and mode justified by sensor datasheet. — *Done when:* analyzer shows correct CPOL/CPHA.
* **123** M ◈ Read WHO_AM_I via SPI and compare to expected value. — *Done when:* ID is correct and wrong mode fails visibly.
* **124** S Respect CS setup and hold times. — *Done when:* timings exist in code and are visible on analyzer.
* **125** M Use DMA for SPI burst with CS asserted throughout. — *Done when:* burst is continuous.
* **126** S Use sensor DRDY/INT pin and transfer only when active. — *Done when:* no stale reads occur.
* **127** M Configure I2C at 100 kHz and 400 kHz with justified pull-up resistors. — *Done when:* rise time is measured or calculated and compatible with baud rate.
* **128** M Handle slave clock stretching. — *Done when:* transfer succeeds with stretching slave.
* **129** M ◈ Recover a stuck I2C bus (9 SCL clock pulses plus stop). — *Done when:* held SDA line is released.
* **130** M ◈ Report NACK within bounded time instead of hanging. — *Done when:* caller receives error within timeout.
* **131** S Use repeated start to read a register. — *Done when:* you demonstrate that intermediate stop breaks the read.
* **132** S Read a 16-bit register with correct byte endianness. — *Done when:* value matches expected.
* **133** M ◈ Enforce timeout on all blocking transfers. — *Done when:* hung device does not hang caller.
* **134** S Interface two SPI devices with separate CS pins. — *Done when:* traffic to one never asserts CS of the other.
* **135** L **Block:** bus_ops interface (read_reg, write_reg, read_burst) abstracting transport; sensor driver tested on host against mock transport. — *Done when:* switching SPI to I2C does not alter application, and NACK/timeout tests pass.
##### Level 13 — Internal flash and persistent configuration
**Prerequisite:** Level 3. **Verified with:** debugger, option bytes, host tests with flash simulator. **Caution:** never set RDP Level 2 on an evaluation board.
* **136** M Erase and program a flash page from application (page size and write granularity per RM0440). — *Done when:* read value matches and erase leaves 0xFF.
* **137** S ◈ Write without prior erase or with invalid size/alignment. — *Done when:* you capture error flags and explain them.
* **138** S Measure CPU stall duration during page erase and its effect on critical ISR. — *Done when:* time is measured and consequence documented.
* **139** M Create configuration record with CRC, version, and dual alternating pages. — *Done when:* cutting power mid-write at 20 different points always preserves a valid configuration.
* **140** S Read option bytes and RDP level. — *Done when:* protection levels table exists and explains why Level 2 is avoided.
* **141** M ◈ Read half-programmed flash area to induce ECC error (if family reports it; check RM0440). — *Done when:* flag or NMI is observed and handled.
* **142** L **Block:** cfgstore module with host tests against flash simulator. — *Done when:* passes in CI, survives simulated power cut, and Capstone C uses it.
##### Level 14 — Structures and memory
**Prerequisite:** Levels 11 and 12. **Verified with:** .map, size, stack watermark.
* **143** M Serialize field-by-field instead of struct memcpy. — *Done when:* byte order is defined and test passes across compilers (clang and gcc).
* **144** S Place read-only tables in flash. — *Done when:* map shows .rodata and RAM does not grow with table size.
* **145** S Use union for register aliases only where safe. — *Done when:* access compiles to single load or store and unsafe conditions are documented.
* **146** M ◈ Create RAM budget: stack, heap, statics, and buffers. — *Done when:* everything fits with margin and every item has an owner.
* **147** S Place hot buffer in CCM and verify in map; check RM0440 if DMA reaches CCM on your family. — *Done when:* map shows section and DMA restriction is recorded.
* **148** M ◈ Detect stack overflow using canary and stack painting. — *Done when:* deep recursion triggers check.
* **149** M Measure worst-case stack depth by painting and counting intact bytes after deepest path. — *Done when:* you have a number and justified margin.
* **150** S Replace large stack buffer with static buffer. — *Done when:* stack watermark improves by measured amount.
* **151** M Document memory map and establish budget as single source of truth. — *Done when:* growing without updating budget breaks build.
* **152** M Relocate DMA buffers to dedicated aligned section. — *Done when:* map justifies each buffer and unaligned placement breaks build.
##### Gate 3 — Capstone C
**Sensor bridge.** One SPI sensor, one I2C sensor, and one ADC channel (Vrefint/internal temperature, or potentiometer) sampled via timer and published over UART in framed packets with CRC at a fixed rate. Rate and calibration are stored in flash via cfgstore. Any sensor can be hot-unplugged: bridge reports loss, continues running, and recovers on reconnect. All transfers have timeouts. Static buffers and registered stack watermark. **Done when:** unplugging each sensor does not freeze bridge, configuration survives reset, parser and NACK/timeout/CRC error paths have CI tests, and RAM budget balances. **Prohibited:** blocking on absent sensor, malloc, or allowing one dead sensor to stall another.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Phase 4 — DMA, core, CAN, power and booting
The phase where you start building systems that survive outside the lab.
##### Level 15 — DMA
**Prerequisite:** Gate 3. **Verified with:** logic analyzer, cycle counter, map. Data cache does not exist on G431KB; cache coherency belongs to Phase 6.
* **153** M Configure memory-to-peripheral DMA channel with correct width and increment, including DMAMUX mapping. — *Done when:* transfer completes and width matches peripheral.
* **154** M ◈ Handle transfer-complete, half-transfer, and transfer error. — *Done when:* forced error is caught and recovered.
* **155** S Keep DMA buffers and stack in separate memory regions. — *Done when:* map justifies it.
* **156** M Process circular buffer in halves (double buffer). — *Done when:* no samples are dropped across wrap.
* **157** M Segment transfers larger than channel counter limit. — *Done when:* large transfer completes in chunks without truncation.
* **158** M Abort channel mid-transfer without corrupting peripheral state. — *Done when:* behavior is tested and documented.
* **159** S Disable channel before reconfiguring. — *Done when:* mid-flight reconfiguration causes no corruption.
* **160** S ◈ Intentionally point DMA to local stack variable. — *Done when:* you observe corruption; all DMA buffers become static afterward.
* **161** M Measure CPU cycles freed by DMA compared to polling. — *Done when:* you report both figures.
* **162** M ◈ Compare memory-to-memory DMA with memcpy across sizes. — *Done when:* cycle count curve shows crossover threshold where DMA wins.
##### Level 16 — Cortex-M core, faults and MPU
**Prerequisite:** Level 15. **Verified with:** fault registers, DWT, ITM, watchpoints. G431KB includes MPU (8 regions; verify in RM0440).
* **163** M ◈ Trigger fault, decode CFSR/HFSR/MMFAR/BFAR, and classify as precise or imprecise. — *Done when:* decoded registers name the root cause.
* **164** M ◈ Induce hard fault by jumping to invalid function pointer and locate stacked PC. — *Done when:* you find offending instruction in disassembly.
* **165** M ◈ Reproduce unaligned access: with CCR.UNALIGN_TRP set, or via LDRD/LDM on odd address. — *Done when:* CFSR.UNALIGNED sets and same access via memcpy succeeds.
* **166** S ◈ Enable DIV_0_TRP and trigger division by zero. — *Done when:* UsageFault is captured.
* **167** M Implement dedicated handlers for MemManage, BusFault, and UsageFault. — *Done when:* each triggered fault routes to its handler.
* **168** M Make fault handler save stack frame and cause into uninitialized RAM (or backup registers) and reset. — *Done when:* after reboot, log identifies prior fault.
* **169** M ◈ Mark memory region read-only via MPU. — *Done when:* write to region raises MemManage with fault address.
* **170** M ◈ Mark stack as eXecute-Never (XN) and leave null page unmapped. — *Done when:* jumping to stack and dereferencing NULL fail immediately.
* **171** S Measure function execution cycles with DWT and confirm with logic analyzer. — *Done when:* both measurements match.
* **172** M Output trace over ITM/SWO without UART. — *Done when:* text appears in debugger console.
* **173** M ◈ Use data watchpoint to catch unexpected memory writer. — *Done when:* offending write instruction is identified.
* **174** S Route unused interrupt vectors to logging handler instead of infinite loop. — *Done when:* spurious interrupt produces log line rather than freeze.
* **175** L **Block:** fault_log module (handler, persistence, and host decoder in tools/). — *Done when:* fault dump is decoded automatically on host.
##### Level 17 — CAN
**Prerequisite:** Levels 15 and 16, second board and transceivers. **Verified with:** logic analyzer, oscilloscope if available.
* **176** M Configure Classic FDCAN at 500 kbit/s with sample point near 87.5%. — *Done when:* second node ACKs and bit timing is hand-calculated and documented.
* **177** M Bidirectional frame exchange between two nodes. — *Done when:* zero packet loss for one minute.
* **178** M Configure hardware acceptance filters. — *Done when:* frames outside filter set are rejected in hardware.
* **179** M Transmit CAN FD with payload > 8 bytes and BRS. — *Done when:* receiver gets full payload with correct DLC.
* **180** M ◈ Trigger bus-off by briefly shorting CANH-CANL and recover. — *Done when:* node enters bus-off and restores communication.
* **181** M ◈ Monitor error counters on perturbed bus. — *Done when:* counters increment and are logged.
* **182** M Periodic frame transmission with missed frame detection. — *Done when:* stopped producer triggers timeout on consumer.
* **183** S ◈ Remove one bus termination resistor. — *Done when:* error counters rise or oscilloscope displays reflections.
* **184** S Decide whether to use remote frames and document rationale. — *Done when:* decision and reason are documented.
* **185** M Write message catalog: ID, DLC, rate, producer, consumer, and timeout. — *Done when:* host test confirms no duplicate IDs exist.
* **186** L **Block:** can_drv and can_msg modules generated from catalog (X-macro or table). — *Done when:* encoding and decoding tests pass on host.
##### Level 18 — Low power
**Prerequisite:** Levels 9 and 16. **Verified with:** µA meter with SWD disconnected. G4 modes: Sleep, Low-power run/sleep, Stop 0, Stop 1, Standby, Shutdown (verify in RM0440; Stop 2 unavailable on this family).
* **187** M Measure baseline current in Run mode at 170 MHz and 16 MHz with SWD disconnected. — *Done when:* both measurements recorded with measurement method described.
* **188** M Enter Sleep and wake via EXTI. — *Done when:* current drops and wake-up functions.
* **189** M Enter Stop 0 and Stop 1; wake via pin or RTC/LPTIM. — *Done when:* current drops by at least one order of magnitude versus Run.
* **190** M Enter Standby and enumerate surviving state. — *Done when:* wake-up acts as reset and backup registers retain data.
* **191** M Preserve timestamp through Standby using RTC and backup register. — *Done when:* time is consistent across multiple sleep cycles.
* **192** M ◈ Disable unused peripheral clocks prior to sleeping. — *Done when:* delta is measured.
* **193** S Set unused GPIOs to analog mode. — *Done when:* current drop is measured.
* **194** S Measure wake-up latency for each sleep mode. — *Done when:* each measurement fits within declared budget.
* **195** M Compute energy per wake cycle and compare two duty-cycle strategies. — *Done when:* choice is justified with numbers.
* **196** S ◈ Leave debug enabled in low power and measure cost. — *Done when:* release build (debug disabled) reaches low targets and debug build does not.
* **197** L **Block:** pm module: mode entry, wake reason, and sleep blockers. — *Done when:* active DMA peripheral blocks Stop in automated test.
##### Level 19 — Bootloader and firmware updates
**Prerequisite:** Levels 13, 16, and 17 (or UART). **Verified with:** board you can brick and recover. With 128 KB flash, allocate ~16 KB bootloader and two slots; verify images fit.
* **198** M Reserve bootloader and application slots in linker. — *Done when:* map shows partitions and app links at designated offset.
* **199** M ◈ Validate CRC and vector table (SP in RAM, reset in flash range) prior to jumping. — *Done when:* corrupted image is rejected.
* **200** S Relocate vector table via SCB->VTOR in application. — *Done when:* interrupts function after jump.
* **201** M Execute clean jump: disable interrupts, de-init peripherals, load MSP, branch to reset vector. — *Done when:* app boots with SysTick disabled.
* **202** M Implement chunked update protocol (UART or CAN) with per-chunk CRC and commit step. — *Done when:* partial update is rejected and complete image boots.
* **203** L ◈ Ensure atomic updates: old image remains valid until new image verifies. — *Done when:* cutting power mid-update at arbitrary points still boots old image.
* **204** M Implement rollback on failed boots counter: app must confirm healthy execution. — *Done when:* three boot failures trigger automatic rollback.
* **205** M Protect bootloader flash region (WRP or MPU). — *Done when:* write attempt from application to bootloader region fails.
* **206** M ◈ Authenticate image with HMAC-SHA256 (or Ed25519 using lightweight library). — *Done when:* tampered image fails validation, and threat model notes what is and isn't covered (e.g. key extraction without RDP).
* **207** S Version images and reject downgrade unless explicit override flag is supplied. — *Done when:* unflagged downgrade is rejected.
* **208** S Record boot cause and active slot on every startup. — *Done when:* log displays both.
* **209** M ◈ Deliberately brick image and document recovery procedure (including ST system bootloader entry). — *Done when:* docs/recovery.md exists and was successfully tested.
##### Gate 4 — Capstone D
**Field-updatable CAN node** (two G431KB boards). The node publishes periodic ADC data via DMA, contains an MPU-protected memory region, persists faults via fault logger, and sleeps in Stop mode between active duty cycles within an energy budget. Updated over CAN or UART through bootloader with atomic updates, authentication, and rollback. **Done when:** each failure path (corrupt image, power loss during update, repeated boot crash, bus-off) was provoked at least once with recorded evidence, and average power meets budget. **Prohibited:** losing original working image, exceeding power budget, or booting unverified image.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Phase 5 — Control, RTOS and quality
##### Level 20 — Fixed-point arithmetic and control
**Prerequisite:** Gate 4. **Verified with:** host simulation, real ADC, logic analyzer.
* **210** M Implement Q15/Q31 multiplication with saturation and rounding. — *Done when:* host test against double shows maximum error < 1 LSB across 10^6 cases.
* **211** S Measure execution cycles of MAC operation in float (M4F FPU) versus Q15. — *Done when:* trade-offs are documented in writing.
* **212** M ◈ Provoke filter overflow due to missing saturation. — *Done when:* wrap is visible and resolved using saturation.
* **213** M Implement first-order IIR and moving average filters in fixed point. — *Done when:* step response measured on ADC matches host simulation.
* **214** M Implement discrete PID controller with anti-windup and output clamping, simulated on host against an RC plant. — *Done when:* simulated response is stable within defined criteria.
* **215** M Execute control loop in periodic timer ISR. — *Done when:* period jitter on logic analyzer is under 1% of period.
* **216** L Control physical plant (PWM, RC filter, ADC): tune PID parameters. — *Done when:* measured overshoot and settling time match simulation.
* **217** M ◈ Handle lost sensor (ADC disconnected or out of range). — *Done when:* loop enters safe state and logs fault.
* **218** L **Block:** pid and fixed modules with host test suites. — *Done when:* pass in CI and Capstone E uses them.
##### Level 21 — RTOS
**Prerequisite:** Levels 18 and 20. **Verified with:** timestamped event trace, high-water marks. Assumes FreeRTOS with static allocation.
* **219** M Integrate FreeRTOS using static allocation (no heap) and tick aligned with timebase. — *Done when:* two tasks blink LEDs and map contains no heap region.
* **220** M Create two tasks with differing priorities communicating over a queue. — *Done when:* consumer receives all messages in order.
* **221** M ◈ Utilize mutex and observe priority inheritance. — *Done when:* visible in execution trace.
* **222** S Defer work from ISR to task using task notification or binary semaphore. — *Done when:* ISR remains short and task executes workload.
* **223** S Use counting semaphore for resource bounds and event group with two conditions. — *Done when:* single condition fails to unblock task.
* **224** S Compare software timer against hardware timer. — *Done when:* jitter of both is measured.
* **225** M Size task stacks using high-water mark tracking. — *Done when:* each stack has justified safety margin.
* **226** S ◈ Trigger stack overflow hook by providing insufficient stack. — *Done when:* hook executes and records event.
* **227** M Measure scheduling latency under load and ISR-to-task latency. — *Done when:* worst-case figure is reported within budget.
* **228** M ◈ Reproduce priority inversion with binary semaphore and fix with mutex. — *Done when:* inversion is reproducible prior to fix and disappears after.
* **229** M Enable tickless idle with Stop mode (Level 18). — *Done when:* measured idle current drops.
* **230** S Document technical justification for RTOS adoption over superloop. — *Done when:* document cites concrete requirements rather than "best practices."
##### Level 22 — Scheduling theory
**Prerequisite:** Level 21. **Verified with:** calculations in notes/.
* **231** M Calculate task set CPU utilization and test against Liu-Layland bound. — *Done when:* calculation is in notes/ and compared against measurement.
* **232** M Assign priorities via Rate Monotonic Scheduling and compare against manual assignment. — *Done when:* choice and rationale are explained.
* **233** M Compute worst-case response time (WCRT) for lowest priority task. — *Done when:* compared against deadline and measured execution.
* **234** M ◈ Construct task set that misses deadline and resolve structurally (not by enlarging buffers). — *Done when:* deadline misses before and meets after.
* **235** M Include blocking time from shared resources in analysis. — *Done when:* calculations reflect blocking terms.
* **236** S Document analysis assumptions and where implementation violates them. — *Done when:* review checklist exists and is applied whenever priorities change.
##### Level 23 — Debugging techniques
**Prerequisite:** Level 21. **Verified with:** custom trace buffer, logic analyzer, debugger, git.
* **237** M Implement lightweight trace buffer: DWT timestamped events in RAM, dumped and visualized on host. — *Done when:* task switches and interrupt entries are plotted on timeline.
* **238** M Correlate logic analyzer capture with trace buffer timeline. — *Done when:* events appear in both in identical sequence.
* **239** M ◈ Catch race condition by halting at wrong moment and write reproduction recipe. — *Done when:* recipe reproduces fault on demand.
* **240** M Automate reproduction recipe into script (GDB/OpenOCD). — *Done when:* script fails identically without human intervention.
* **241** S Bisect regression using git bisect run. — *Done when:* first bad commit is identified.
* **242** S Inspect disassembly of critical loop to analyze compiler transformations. — *Done when:* transformation is described.
* **243** S Verify actual buffer contents in memory view. — *Done when:* discrepancy between expectation and reality is caught.
* **244** S Trigger capture on error condition rather than live inspection. — *Done when:* error is captured autonomously.
* **245** S Reduce bug to minimal reproduction under 50 lines before editing suspect code. — *Done when:* commit message identifies root cause.
##### Level 24 — Quality: verification, static analysis and CI
**Prerequisite:** Level 2 and all prior levels. **Verified with:** pipeline and test coverage.
* **246** M Measure branch coverage (gcov/lcov) on host and identify critical untested branch. — *Done when:* test is added and branch is covered.
* **247** M ◈ Write tests for failure paths: NACK, timeout, overrun, and CRC errors. — *Done when:* each has a test demonstrating recovery.
* **248** M ◈ Write HIL test (physical board plus host test harness) for timing-critical path. — *Done when:* test catches intentional regression.
* **249** S Run test suite under -O0 and production optimization level. — *Done when:* both pass or discrepancies are explained.
* **250** M Apply MISRA-C subset using available tooling, with documented deviations. — *Done when:* each deviation has a one-line justification.
* **251** S Audit static analysis suppressions and remove obsolete entries. — *Done when:* every remaining suppression has documented rationale.
* **252** M Complete CI pipeline: build, host tests, and static analysis on every push; enforce size budget and dual builds (target and host). — *Done when:* breaking any condition blocks push.
* **253** M ◈ Enforce pipeline as sole path to flashable image: identical bit-for-bit target builds, archived binary and map, release tags only from green runs. — *Done when:* non-pipeline binary is rejected.
* **254** S Keep secrets and serial numbers out of repository. — *Done when:* pipeline injects credentials and git log remains sanitized.
##### Gate 5 — Capstone E
**A system you would ship.** Take Capstone D node and add physical PID loop (PWM, RC filter, ADC) running under FreeRTOS with analyzed task set. Setpoint and telemetry sent over CAN. Identified and eliminated at least one missed deadline. Fault logger survives reset. Host tests cover parser, error paths, and PID loop. Static analysis clean in CI. Pipeline serves as single path to release binaries. Caught race condition documented with reproducible recipe. **Done when:** third party can clone repo, execute pipeline, and flash working image matching docs/. **Prohibited:** non-pipeline binary, deadline met solely by "running fast enough," or tests that ignore failure branches.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Phase 6 — Dual-core and cache (optional)
Only with NUCLEO-H755ZI-Q. Undertake this phase when you have an explicit project requirement.
##### Level 25 — Dual-core and cache on H755
**Prerequisite:** Gate 5. **Verified with:** debugger, DWT, logic analyzer, map.
* **255** L Boot Cortex-M7 with custom startup and linker (regions, TCM, AXI SRAM, flash). — *Done when:* M7 runs blinky and map documents every region.
* **256** M ◈ Enable L1 caches and reproduce stale read after DMA and non-visible write. — *Done when:* fixed using invalidate (read) and clean (write).
* **257** M ◈ Align DMA buffers to cache line boundaries and pad to complete lines. — *Done when:* cache invalidate does not corrupt neighboring data.
* **258** M Configure MPU non-cacheable region for DMA buffers. — *Done when:* evaluated against manual cache management.
* **259** M Boot Cortex-M4 from Cortex-M7 with valid boot address and clocks. — *Done when:* M4 signals operational status.
* **260** M ◈ Synchronize access to shared peripheral using hardware semaphores (HSEM). — *Done when:* both cores compete without race conditions or corruption.
* **261** M Exchange 10^6 messages through SPSC ring in shared inter-core SRAM. — *Done when:* zero loss; region is non-cacheable or coherency managed.
* **262** S Explicitly assign peripherals to cores by architectural design. — *Done when:* matrix exists and no peripheral is claimed twice.
* **263** M ◈ Halt Cortex-M7 in debugger without stopping Cortex-M4 execution. — *Done when:* M4 continues uninterrupted.
* **264** M Measure inter-core communication latency and jitter. — *Done when:* both figures are quantified.
* **265** M ◈ Detect crash of other core and transition to safe state. — *Done when:* killing active core triggers safe state.
* **266** S Reimplement prior single-core exercise using two cores. — *Done when:* documented justification explains what second core added.
##### Capstone F (optional)
**Dual-core application with cache-coherent DMA pipeline.** One core acquires sensor data via DMA with caches enabled; second core processes and transmits data. Cores communicate over SPSC queue in shared SRAM. **Done when:** 10^6 messages without corruption, empirical proof that cache maintenance was required (disabling maintenance yields stale data), and safe failover if either core halts. **Prohibited:** unaligned DMA buffers or declaring "works in debugger" as sufficient verification.

#### Appendix A — Anti-patterns this plan aims to unlearn
Read before each phase.
1. **Busy-waiting with dummy loop** (for (i=0;i<1e6;i++)). Use timebase.
2. **HAL_Delay in an ISR.** Freezes the timing source being waited upon.
3. **Runtime malloc.** Use static pools and buffers.
4. **volatile as atomic substitute.** It is not (Level 7).
5. **printf inside an ISR.** Queue event and process outside interrupt context.
6. **Ignoring return values.** status_t exists for a reason.
7. **Pointer casts for parsing.** Use memcpy and explicit serialization.
8. **Switch statement ignoring illegal events.** Log and increment error counter (Level 8).
9. **Forgetting to clear pending interrupt bit.** ISR loops infinitely.
10. **DMA buffers on stack.** Static and properly aligned.
11. **Timeout comparison without wrap handling.** Compare with subtraction, never with >.
12. **Blocking bus operations without timeout.** Unresponsive slave must not freeze host.
13. **Flash erase ignoring ISR execution.** Erase halts execution from flash.
14. **PID controller without anti-windup.** Integrator saturates and delays recovery.
15. **Floats in ISR without FPU context awareness.** Enable FPU and understand automatic stacking.
16. **RDP Level 2 on development board.** Permanent lock with no return.
17. **Measuring current with active debugger connection.** Measures debugger power overhead.
18. **Firmware binary existing only on local laptop.** If it didn't come from CI, it doesn't exist.
19. **Copying CubeMX output blindly.** Use it to inspect register sequences, not as replacement.
20. **Tests that pass by testing nothing.** Break test intentionally to verify it fails.

#### Appendix B — Instrumentation by phase
| Phase | Minimum Required |
| ------ | ------ |
| 1 | board, USB cable, toolchain, git |
| 2 | logic analyzer, multimeter |
| 3 | second board (pulse generator), SPI and I2C sensors |
| 4 | CAN transceivers, terminators, µA meter |
| 5 | same plus RC circuit (resistor + capacitor) |
| 6 | NUCLEO-H755ZI-Q |

#### Appendix C — Readings
* RM0440 (STM32G4 reference manual), PM0214 (Cortex-M4 programming manual), G431KB datasheet, UM2397 (Nucleo-32 manual).
* Joseph Yiu, *The Definitive Guide to ARM Cortex-M3 and Cortex-M4 Processors*.
* Elecia White, *Making Embedded Systems*.
* Barr Group, *Embedded C Coding Standard*.
* Liu and Layland (1973), scheduling algorithms for multiprogramming in a hard-real-time environment.
* FreeRTOS Documentation (static allocation, tickless idle).

#### Appendix D — Out of scope (intentional)
USB, Ethernet, Bluetooth/Wi-Fi, displays/graphics (LCD/TFT), embedded Linux, functional safety certification (IEC 61508, ISO 26262 beyond MISRA), advanced DSP beyond Level 20, and full system security (hardware secure boot). These are worthy next steps, but belong after this curriculum.

#### Appendix E — Mapping against FPGA roadmap
| FPGA Roadmap | Equivalent in this Curriculum |
| ------ | ------ |
| Levels 1-2 (logic gates, combinational) | Levels 1 and 4 (C, bitwise, GPIO) |
| Level 3 (sequential logic) | Levels 5 and 9 (time, timers) |
| Level 4 (counters) | Level 9 (timers and input capture) |
| Level 5 (FSM) | Level 8 (state machines) |
| Level 6 (memories) | Levels 13 and 14 (flash, memory) |
| Level 7 (UART, SPI, I2C, PWM, debouncer) | Levels 6, 9, 11, and 12 |
| Level 8 (FIFOs, arbiters, DMA) | Levels 7 and 15 (ring buffer, DMA) |
| Level 9 (CPU architecture) | Level 16 (core internals) |
| Level 10 (CDC, watchdog, interrupts) | Levels 5, 9, and 18 |
| Levels 11-12 (verification) | Levels 2 and 24 (tests, HIL, CI) |
